messages.subject: findNextItem for dummies (Help!)
parts:
I'm a software developer with very little domain knowledge.  (It's murky cat to me).  

The documentation made it seem like findNextItem() did what I needed, but its apparently not that simple. (Possibly I need to undertstand and use local_pattern instead?)  .

I was given an R script that was essentially just setting parameters and a single call to mirtCAT:

shinySurvey <- function(questions, options) {
df <- data.frame(
Question = questions
          Option = options,
          Type = “radio”, stringsAsFactors = F)
result <- mirtCAT(df, design_elements=FALSE, <otherParameters>)
result
}

which administers a survey via shiny UI.

My task is administer the exact same survey to users of our EMA mobile app.  I need to implement the functions buildInitialState and updateState  so that

runSurvey <- function(questions, options) {
state <- buildInitialState(questions, options)
while( !is.na(state$next_item_ix) {
response <- ask(
prompt = questions[state$next_item_ix], 
opts = options[state$next_item_ix. ])
state <- updateState(state, response)
}
state
}

will yield a final state such that   
        
runSurvey(questions, options)$result == shinySurvey(questions, options)

for all sequences of actual responses.

I  have an implementation, but it’s not yield the same sequence & not terminating.  I am not including it in this initial post since I’m hoping the solution is something simple & my code is structured a little differently.
